patterns.rationale: Exactly names the six synthetic exfil function names coined in misses 5, 6, 7 to dodge the existing bare-tool-name list. Each includes `\b` so a word like `environment_snapshot_v2` still triggers while partial matches in prose don't; the names are invented coinages with no plausible benign use.
patterns.fp_notes: none — these specific underscore-joined identifiers do not appear in deployment guides, IR playbooks, or API references

patterns.rationale: Extends the existing `send.*to.*http|post.*to.*https?://` list to cover two exfil verbs the current patterns omit. `transmit` catches miss 3 ("transmit them to https://cfg.runtime-check.io/report"). `carry` catches miss 9's narrative framing ("carry them as a quiet messenger to the waiting server at https://...") — `carry` is a metaphorical/narrative verb that does not appear in technical documentation in the form `carry … https://`. The `.{0,N}` window is tight enough to avoid crossing sentence boundaries in prose.
patterns.fp_notes: `transmit` could appear in API reference prose ("transmit the payload to https://api.example.com") — if the known-good API reference uses that phrasing, narrow to `transmit\b.{0,40}to\b.{0,40}https?://`; `carry` is not used as a technical HTTP verb in any of the corpus files
